query: GPU cloud provider raises or cuts GPU rental prices per hour

results.title: Your GPU provider can re-price your workloads with two weeks' notice. Nebius just did — again. | Peter Lee
highlights:
On September 17, Nebius told customers that pay-as-you-go GPU rates rise October 1: H100s from $3.85 to $4.50/hr (+17%), B300s to $9.50 (+21%), CPU +25%, and memory-backed instances +41%. It's their second hike in three months.

Two things worth noting:
First, the steepest increase isn't on GPUs — it's memory (+41%). The binding constraint on AI compute right now isn't silicon, it's memory and the megawatts to run it. That's why even four-year-old H100s are getting more expensive to rent, not cheaper.

Second, the market loved it. NBIS jumped ~9% on the news. Investors read it as pricing power — capacity rationing, not distress. When your customers have nowhere else to go, you can move the rate card twice a quarter.
This is the FinOps lesson I keep coming back to: in GPU land, price predictability is becoming a genuine differentiator. The cheapest $/GPU-hr means nothing if the number changes before your budget cycle ends.

results.title: Nebius Raised Inference Prices 18.3%, Not Cut Them – Trades Prophet

The AI cloud company is lifting prices on Token Factory, its managed inference platform, by an average of 18.3% on pay-as-you-go dedicated endpoints, with B300 capacity rising 20% from $8.10 to $9.70 an hour, according to customer communications posted publicly and reported by Stocktwits on 23 September. Nebius has not formally announced the change. The stock closed at $243.48 on 24 September, within sight of a $299.86 52-week high against a $73.52 low.

A caveat that deserves more attention than it has received: this increase has reached customers but not the tape. Nebius has issued no press release and made no filing, and the reporting rests on screenshots of customer communications. For a Nasdaq-listed issuer whose entire equity story is pricing power, that is an odd place to leave a material commercial change — and it means the first authoritative confirmation will probably arrive on the third-quarter call rather than in a disclosure document. Treat the specific per-hour numbers as well-sourced but unconfirmed until then.

results.title: GPU rents rise 17–21% on 1 October while the neoclouds' own loan documents show borrowing 100bp dearer
highlights: The pricing half of the thesis is verifiable at source, which is the most useful thing here. Nebius's own pricing page carries two columns — current, and effective 1 October 2026 — showing on-demand per-GPU-hour rates going from $3.85 to $4.50 for H100, $4.50 to $5.40 for H200, $7.15 to $8.50 for B200 and $7.85 to $9.50 for B300. Those are increases of 16.9%, 20.0%, 18.9% and 21.0%. Roundups describing this as up to 21% are accurate; the table is better, because it says which chip and from what. It is a rate card, not a revenue disclosure — what Nebius intends to charge, not what it will collect.

Nebius's GPU Price Hike Attacks the Fear That's Hung Over AI Cloud | AInvest
highlights:
Nebius (NBIS) will raise prices on its on-demand GPU cloud services by around 20% starting on Oct. 1, touching Nvidia's H100, H200, B200, and B300 accelerators - the chips AI developers rent to train their models. This is the whole of Nebius's business: a cloud that buys Nvidia hardware in volume and rents the compute back out. Shares have climbed all week on the news, closing up about 7% on Thursday at $243.48.

A vendor does not announce a price increase on capacity nobody wants. The hike is a direct statement about supply and demand in a market whose bear case has always been oversupply. If a glut of idle Nvidia clusters were about to undercut each other to zero, raising prices into it would be the wrong move; that Nebius believes it can charge more for its most sought-after chips is evidence that buyers, not sellers, hold the bargaining power right now.

results.title: Neocloud vs Hyperscaler: The real total cost of ownership in 2026 | AI Compute Marketplace | Compare GPU Cloud & Data Centers | ComputeStacker Insights
highlights:
## Key Takeaways

- Neoclouds’ on-demand H100 pricing ranges between $3.99 and $6.16/GPU/hour, whereas hyperscalers range between $6.88 and $12.29/GPU/hour.
- Lambda is the cheapest at $3.99/GPU/hour compared to other pricing on its currently live pricing page; correcting for out-of-date pricing figures showing $2.99 elsewhere.
- Neoclouds do not charge any egress costs; AWS charges around $0.09/GB beyond a 100GB free tier.
- Based on an 8 GPU instance over 30 days, CoreWeave and Lambda together make up around half to a third of Azure’s cost, including egress costs.
- Even AWS’s reserved pricing helps close the gap: a three-year commitment brings down its on-demand price by 57%, almost to Lambda’s on-demand price.
- There is still a premium for compliance certifications, customer support, and existing enterprise deals that neo-clouds lack.

...

## GPU Cloud Pricing: Neoclouds vs Hyperscalers at a glance

Here’s what a single on-demand NVIDIA H100 costs across five major providers, as of late September 2026:

| Provider | Type | On-demand rate (per GPU-hour) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lambda | Neocloud | ~$3.99 |
| CoreWeave | Neocloud | $4.25–$6.16 (varies by product tier — see below) |
| AWS | Hyperscaler | $6.88 |
| GCP | Hyperscaler | $11.06 |
| Azure | Hyperscaler | $12.29 |

The spread is real. At the extremes, Azure’s on-demand rate runs roughly three times Lambda’s.

But a sticker-price table only tells you what an hour of compute costs. It doesn’t say what a month of usage actually costs once egress, idle time, and support get added in. The next three sections work through each of those pieces.

...

Prices are increasing in other regions. Some trackers present the same instance as being available for over $11 per hour outside the US. Reserved one-year and three-year terms reduce the on-demand price by about 20 to 57% depending on the term.

...

The reserved pricing plan saves even more money. If you make a one-year upfront commitment, you can bring down the price to $5.42 per hour, or 21%. If you opt for a three-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan, the price will drop ‌to $2.97 per hour; that’s 57% off and very close to Lambda.

...

The hourly price is the headline, but not the full story.

Outgoing Data Transfer. AWS will charge you for data transferred out of its network beyond a monthly free threshold, at $0.09 per GB until the first 10 TB. This is according to Cloudflare’s calculation of AWS’s outgoing data transfer pricing rates, confirmed by 7 other independent trackers.

Lambda and CoreWeave both state on their pricing pages that there’s no fee for outgoing data transfers. If your team ‌routinely exporting trained checkpoints or datasets, this discrepancy can add up quickly.

Idle Time and Minimum Commitments. A reserved but idle GPU will incur a charge – one of the biggest discrepancies between advertised price and true cost. We’ve detailed the whole story in our hidden costs of GPU cloud article.

Provisioning Delay. Even if availability doesn’t directly change profits, it can still affect spending. According to an article that cites CoreWeave’s Q1 2026 earnings call, the company’s CFO had this to say regarding their capacity and provisioning delays.

results.title: Best GPU Cloud Providers for AI (2026): 10 Compared
highlights:
A GPU cloud rents you graphics processors by the hour so you can train, fine-tune or run AI models without buying hardware. There are three kinds. Hyperscalers (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure) sell GPUs next to hundreds of other services. Neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Together AI) are built only for AI workloads. Marketplaces and serverless platforms (RunPod, Vast.ai, Modal) make it easy to grab one GPU for an hour.

To compare fairly, we priced the same chip everywhere: the NVIDIA H100 80GB, on-demand, per GPU-hour, in US regions where the page states one, checked on 25 September 2026. The spread is huge: from about $1.73 on the Vast.ai marketplace to $12.29 on Azure, roughly seven times more for the same GPU. We also used SemiAnalysis's independent ClusterMAX 3.0 reliability ratings (23 September 2026) to judge how well each provider runs large clusters.

...

Nebius is the best GPU cloud provider for most AI teams in September 2026. It holds SemiAnalysis's top Platinum reliability rating, publishes per-GPU on-demand prices (H100 $3.85 per GPU-hour, rising to $4.50 on 1 October 2026) and offers the newest Blackwell GPUs. Pick RunPod for the cheapest easy H100s ($2.69 Community Cloud, $3.49 Secure Cloud), CoreWeave for large training clusters, Lambda for simple on-demand instances, and Modal for serverless GPUs billed by the second.

results.title: H100 Rental Prices Halve to $3.38/Hr in 2026 · Slicast
highlights:
R enting an Nvidia H100 for an hour costs anywhere from $1.49 to nearly $13 in September 2026, depending on who you ask and which cloud you pick. That spread, once a rounding error in a niche market, has become one of the clearest signals of how tight the AI compute supply chain still is, two years after ChatGPT turned GPU capacity into a boardroom talking point. Pricing trackers, bank analysts, and Nvidia's own executives are now telling three overlapping stories at once: H100 rental costs have fallen by roughly half since early 2024, newer chips like the H200 and B200 command a steep premium, and the entire market remains bottlenecked by memory, not by silicon.

...

Pricing tracker Thunder Compute, in a blog post on H100 pricing dated September 1, 2026, lists on-demand H100 80GB rates spanning from $2.89 an hour on RunPod up to $10.98 an hour on Google Cloud's a3-highgpu-8g instances. CloudZero's H100 cost breakdown, published in late August 2026, puts the full spread even wider: Vast.ai as low as $1.49 an hour, Azure as high as $6.98 per GPU-hour on demand. Between those two data points sits a real number that infrastructure teams have to budget against every quarter.

Three tiers have emerged in the market and they behave almost like separate products. Marketplace and community-cloud rates sit at the floor, where platforms like RunPod's community tier and Vast.ai's peer-to-peer listings undercut everyone else. Specialist clouds such as Lambda, Nebius, and Crusoe occupy the middle, offering more reliability and support without hyperscaler markup. Hyperscaler on-demand pricing from AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud sits at the top, often two to four times the marketplace floor for the exact same chip. H100 80GB pricing ranges from $1.49–$2.99 per hour on marketplace floors, $3.19–$4.59 on specialist clouds, and $6.88–$10.98 on hyperscalers. H200 141GB runs $3.59 per hour on RunPod Community, $4.31–$4.59 on specialist clouds, and $5.58–$6.35 on hyperscalers. B200 data remains least reliable, with limited public marketplace data around $5.89 per hour cited from RunPod and specialist estimates reaching $8.64 per hour.

...

AIMultiple's Cloud GPU Rental Price Index, updated August 25, 2026, found that the median H100 rental price across its tracked cohort now sits around $3.38 an hour, down from more than $7 an hour in early 2024. That is a genuine price collapse of over half in just two and a half years, and it reflects the normal pattern for an aging chip: more supply comes online, more providers compete for the same customers, and rates fall. A separate tracker tells a similar story from a slightly later vantage point: the Mercatus GPU Index, measured September 13, 2026, put the average H100 rate at $3.84 an hour across 27 tracked providers, with Lambda listing $3.99 an hour, a reminder that the exact figure depends heavily on which cohort and which averaging method a tracker uses.

results.title: Reserve B200 or B300 GPUs and Tune Your Inference Setup
highlights:
A Prime Inference reservation includes, per the Prime Inference page:

- Blackwell hardware. GMI Cloud benchmarked "tuned per-model runtimes on B200, B300, and GB200 NVL72." B300 is offered through Prime Inference; reserved B300 pricing comes from GMI Cloud sales.
- Reservation terms. "There is no minimum contract. On-demand billing is hourly per GPU, with no per-token markup and no shared-pool surge pricing. For sustained production workloads, reserved capacity is available on a seasonal basis or annually at lower per-hour rates."
- Tuning. "Per-model kernel, scheduling, and routing optimization," with "Quantization configurable. Multi-GPU orchestration handled."
- Validation before commitment. "Qualified prospects also receive free GPU-hour trial credits to validate performance against their own workload." Ask GMI Cloud sales to confirm eligibility when you share the sizing brief described below.
- Your weights. "Any open-source, fine-tuned, or proprietary weights," loaded from Hugging Face, S3, or your own storage.

For reference pricing on the hardware itself, GMI Cloud's GPU page lists the NVIDIA B200 "from $4.00/GPU-hour" with a Limited Availability tag, as of September 2026. That is a GPU compute list price, not a Prime Inference quote.

The pricing page has no B300 hourly rate, so B300 is quoted by sales.

results.title: Nebius повысила цены на инференс на 18,3%, а не снизила их. | Новости Gate | Gate News
highlights:
- Nebius повысила цены на инференс в Token Factory в среднем на 18,3% с 1 октября 2026 года.
- Стоимость мощности B300 выросла на 20% — с 8,10 до 9,70 доллара в час; цены на H100, H200 и B200 также повысились.
- Nebius сообщила, что годовая стоимость контрактов по основным сделкам в сфере ИИ-облака составляет 20–25 млн долларов за мегаватт, а спотовые цены — 40–50 млн долларов за мегаватт.

Nebius повысила цены на Token Factory — свою управляемую платформу для инференса — в среднем на 18,3% для выделенных конечных точек с оплатой по мере использования; новые цены действуют с 1 октября. Об этом говорится в опубликованных сообщениях для клиентов, о которых Stocktwits сообщил 23 сентября. Стоимость мощности B300 выросла на 20% — с 8,10 до 9,70 доллара в час; также подорожали уровни H100, H200 и B200. Nebius официально об этом изменении не объявляла. Повышение отражает дефицит энергетических мощностей дата-центров, а не стоимость кремниевых чипов: в письме акционерам за второй квартал компания, занимающаяся облачными решениями для ИИ, раскрыла, что годовая сумма контрактов на базовые облачные мощности для ИИ составляет 20–25 млн долларов за мегаватт, тогда как краткосрочные и аукционные сделки демонстрируют ценовой потенциал в диапазоне 40–50 млн долларов за мегаватт — двукратную разницу между долгосрочными и спотовыми ценами.

...

Цены на выделенные конечные точки Token Factory с оплатой по мере использования выросли в среднем на 18,3% с 1 октября. Почасовые ставки увеличились с 4,05 до 4,70 доллара для H100 (+16%), с 4,70 до 5,60 доллара для H200 (+19%), с 7,40 до 8,70 доллара для B200 (+18%) и с 8,10 до 9,70 доллара для B300 (+20%), согласно сообщениям для клиентов, о которых Stocktwits сообщил 23 сентября. Nebius не делала официального объявления. 24 сентября акции компании закрылись на отметке 243,48 доллара — недалеко от годового максимума 299,86 доллара и при минимуме 73,52 доллара.

...

В конце августа Nebius завершила частное размещение старших конвертируемых облигаций, привлекая около 5,75 млрд долларов и увеличив первоначальный объём сделки с 4,5 млрд долларов. CME готовится запустить фьючерсы на ставки аренды GPU, а Kalshi уже несколько месяцев формирует форвардные кривые для вычислительных мощностей. В сочетании с квартальными капитальными затратами в размере 5,7 млрд долларов предоплаты необходимы, а не просто улучшают показатели, говорится в анализе. Бизнес стал достаточно крупным, чтобы ценовой и финансовый циклы шли одновременно, однако их продолжительность различается.
